speaker: Doctor
text: I'm sorry to hear you're experiencing sudden vertigo. To better understand your condition, can you describe how long this episode has been lasting, and do you feel any nausea or hearing changes along with the dizziness? Also, have you noticed any recent head injuries or high blood pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details; the brief duration and sudden onset are helpful clues. Did you notice any new hearing loss, tinnitus, or ringing in your ears during that episode? Also, please tell me if you experienced any weakness, numbness, slurred speech, or double vision alongside the dizziness.

REQUEST TEST: Basic Metabolic Panel, Complete Blood Count, Lipid Panel, Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH)

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Gastroenteritis typically causes systemic symptoms like fever and abdominal cramping, not isolated sudden spinning vertigo; can you clarify if your dizziness was strictly positional or constant, and did you experience any limb weakness or facial drooping during the episode? I am also ordering a Basic Metabolic Panel and Complete Blood Count to rule out metabolic causes.

REQUEST TEST: Basic Metabolic Panel, Complete Blood Count

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the sudden onset, duration of only 3 minutes, and your age, I need to rule out a transient ischemic attack (TIA) or stroke. Did you experience any slurred speech, facial drooping, or weakness in your arms or legs during that episode? Also, did the vertigo resolve completely once you stopped the spinning motion?

REQUEST TEST: CT_Head_NonContrast, MRI_Brain

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
